# Fireworks raises GPU rates up to 30%

09/01/26, 10:35 AM

 Follows up on Owning a Model Costs $124K per Benchmark Point 

Earlier analysis of Fireworks’ Training API argued that a narrow team should train its own model only when specialization pays back roughly $124,000 per benchmark point plus engineering cost. Fireworks’ current on-demand price table raises H100/H200 from $7 to $8 per GPU-hour, B200 from $10 to $13, B300 from $12 to $15, and GB300 from $18 to $20 starting September 1—an 11%–30% increase. The call holds: dedicated reinforcement training still belongs to a narrow buyer set, but new runs should use the higher rates because Fireworks prices reinforcement fine-tuning by GPU-hour.

# Upcoming SaladCloud Price Changes: September 12, 2026

SaladCloud GPU and vCPU pricing is changing on September 12, 2026: 15 GPU classes drop 25% on average, while RTX 5090 and 4090 prices increase.

Jared Carpenter

Product Update SaladCloud Tue Sep 01 2026

We're updating GPU and vCPU pricing on SaladCloud to correct places where our prices had drifted out of line with demand: some classes were priced above what the market will bear, and a couple were priced below it.

These changes take effect Saturday, September 12, 2026 at 00:00 UTC, and they will impact active and running instances at that time.

## Summary Copy Anchor Link

- Prices for 15 GPU classes are coming down, by 25% on average at High Priority (individual classes fall between 16% and 38%).
- Lowest Priority pricing is staying stable, with the exception of the RTX 5080, where it comes down from $0.180 to $0.150.
- RTX 5090 and RTX 4090: we've had to raise High, Medium, and Low Priority prices on these two classes. At High Priority, the RTX 5090 moves from $0.450 to $0.500 and the RTX 4090 from $0.300 to $0.330.
- For CPU-only workloads, vCPU pricing is going up from $0.004 to $0.005 per vCPU per hour. RAM pricing is unchanged. GPU container groups aren't charged for vCPU or RAM.
- Every GPU class not listed below is unchanged.

results.title: Nebius, Oracle, and Vessl AI Push AI Rental Rates Higher as Delivery Tightens | Drip
highlights:
## What is this trend?

GPU rental rates are rising as cloud and AI operators pass through higher costs for power, cooling, and delivery constraints on already-contracted capacity.

- • Nebius, Oracle, and Vessl AI are raising prices on specific GPU offerings, not the whole market.
- • Scarcity is shifting from chips alone to deliverable capacity: power, cooling, and site readiness.
- • Utility delays and high-density racks are making retrofits and interconnects a billable constraint.
- • Operators with power and thermal control can command higher rents and better margins.
- • Pricing is fragmenting by region and SKU as guaranteed access becomes more valuable than headline supply.

## What’s the latest?

September 28, 2026

Nebius raised selected Nvidia GPU rates 17%–21%, Oracle renewed expiring GPU contracts about 20% higher, and Vessl AI lifted H100 pricing in Korea by 24.7%, where local H100 rentals were up 21.9% month over month to $3.2

highlights:
# The four public GPU floors we track held again this week: H100 $3.85, H200 $4.29, B200 $6.69, A100 $2.30, the lowest reviewed public on-demand rate per family (August 30, 2026). Underneath them … | Bobby Clay · LinkedIn · 2026-09-01T00:00:00+00:00

**Bobby Clay**.

---

The four public GPU floors we track held again this week: H100 $3.85, H200 $4.29, B200 $6.69, A100 $2.30, the lowest reviewed public on-demand rate per family (August 30, 2026). Underneath them the transaction-based OCPI kept moving, on all four families, with the B200 index down 8.9% (Ornn x ICE, August 30). A held floor beside a falling index is a point-in-time gap, not a price cut.

The real motion was in the map, not the price. AWS listed its eight-GPU B300 (p6-b300.48xlarge) in two more public catalog markets this week, Hyderabad and Sao Paulo, bringing it to five AWS regions in our reviewed catalog. Across the clouds we track, publicly listed on-demand B300 now spans from about $7.85 (Nebius) to about $35.62 (AWS) per GPU-hour (August 30, 2026), up from about $7.85 to $26.15 a week ago as AWS added Sao Paulo. A catalog listing is not proof the instance is orderable, but the map is filling in faster than the price is settling.

results.title: Computable GPU Index Review (2026): Pricing, Features & Honest Verdict - MakerStack
highlights:
## What is Computable GPU Index?

CGI is a price index for renting GPUs. Every 15 minutes it collects the published on-demand rental rates of a fixed panel of providers, takes an interquantile mean over weighted votes, and prints one number in USD per GPU-hour for each accelerator it covers. H100, H200, B200 and B300 are live. On 1 September 2026 at 11:30 UTC it read $7.70 for the B300, $6.64 for the B200, $4.19 for the H200 SXM and $3.43 for the H100 SXM.

The point is not the number, it is the receipts. Every data point is sourced and timestamped, the calculation is in a public Python repository, and there is a `./reproduce h100 2026-09-01` command that re-derives a full day from raw public history and exits 0 only if every value and digest matches what was published. The index is served four ways, all free: a live page, an anonymous read-only REST API with no key, a flat-file corpus, and an MCP server at mcp.getcomputable.com/mcp that any agent can query. It launched on Product Hunt on 1 September 2026 and took second place with 185 upvotes.

...

Silicon Data is the established competitor and the direct comparison is instructive. It publishes an H100 rental price index on a Bloomberg ticker, SDH100RT, standardised for rental term, cluster scale and interconnect, with separate neo-cloud and hyperscaler readings. Its neo-cloud H100 reading is $2.53 per GPU-hour against Computable’s $3.43 on-demand print for the same accelerator, which tells you how much the panel and the standardisation rules decide the answer. Basic is free with 30 days of history, Pro is $998 a month with a 7-day trial, Enterprise is quoted per organisation. It is the pick if you need history, breadth and a ticker; CGI is the pick if you need the calculation itself.

highlights:
B200 from $4.25/hr, RTX 4090 from $0.39/hr. Hourly, no contract.

Hyperstack (a NexGen Cloud brand) is a UK-headquartered GPU cloud with capacity in Canada, Norway and Europe. It has a clean per-GPU rate card, reservation discounts, free egress, per-minute billing and a reputation for responsive support. Its lineup runs from RTX A4000 to HGX B200 and B300, and it lists the RTX Pro 6000 Server Edition, which makes it one of the few direct comparators for packet.ai's most popular SKU.

...

### What Hyperstack offers

Hyperstack's published on-demand rates: RTX Pro 6000 SE (96GB) $1.85/hr, H200 SXM $3.99/hr, H100 SXM $3.20/hr, H100 PCIe $2.50/hr (NVLink variant $2.60/hr), A100 SXM 80GB $1.60/hr, L40 (48GB) $1.00/hr, RTX A6000 $0.50/hr, RTX A4000 $0.15/hr. HGX B200 is listed around $6.00/hr. Reservations start at $1.30/hr for the RTX Pro 6000, $1.75/hr for H100 PCIe and $2.79/hr for H200.

- Per-minute billing, free egress, hibernation to pause instances without losing state
- Reservation pricing on 1–3 year terms brings most cards down 20–30%
- Regions in Canada, Norway and mainland Europe; no US on-demand capacity listed
- Also runs an AI Studio for per-token LLM inference and fine-tuning

...

Hyperstack's on-demand rates are already sharp, and its reservation tiers push several cards lower still. The gap between the two platforms is narrower here than against most other comparisons on this list. What separates them is geography: Hyperstack has no listed US on-demand capacity, running out of Canada, Norway and mainland Europe. packet.ai runs both US and EU on-demand.

On the two cards that overlap most directly, the RTX Pro 6000 and B200, the comparison depends on which Hyperstack tier you use. Against Hyperstack's on-demand RTX Pro 6000 SE at $1.85/hr, packet.ai's RTX 6000 Pro Dynamic at $0.76/hr is 59% lower. Against Hyperstack's reserved rate of $1.30/hr, the gap is still 42%. On B200, Hyperstack's roughly $6.00/hr on-demand compares to packet.ai's $4.25/hr Dynamic, a 29% gap.

- Dynamic: scheduler-enforced multi-tenant, US and EU on-demand. RTX 6000 Pro at $0.76/hr, B200 at $4.25/hr. No reservation required to get the lower rate.
- Dedicated: a whole card, single-tenant, 99% SLA. RTX 4090 at $0.39/hr, B200 at $7.99/hr (also 2×, 3× and 8× nodes). The A100 80GB ($0.89/hr) is Dynamic only; the L40S is coming soon.

...

Billing is hourly; the one monthly plan is 2× B200 Dedicated at $11,665.40/mo. There are no platform fees and no ingress charges; egress is $0.04/GB. Up to 2 TB of local NVMe per node is included. Dynamic instances are SSH-ready in under five minutes, Dedicated in five to ten. Capacity is live in the US (California, Virginia, Texas, Oregon) and Europe (Frankfurt, Amsterdam, Paris, London, Dublin). H100 SXM, H200 and RTX 5090 are on the notify list.

Hyperstack is a well-run European neocloud with fair prices and good support. packet.ai is simply cheaper on the cards they share, dramatically so on the RTX Pro 6000, and it has US capacity Hyperstack lacks. results.title: On-demand vs spot GPU cloud pricing | GPUBeacon
highlights:
GPU Cloud News still treats “$X/hr” as one product. It is not. On-demand is a published hour you can start. Spot is a bid against leftover capacity. Reserved is a contract. A quote is a meeting. If a GPU cloud mixes those in one table, the cheapest cell is usually the one you cannot run.

...

## On-demand is the product

On-demand means you pay the listed hourly rate and the machine is yours until you stop it, within the provider’s actual policy. No bid. No “maybe later.” No 12-month commit hiding in a footnote. That is the hour I compare across Vast.ai, RunPod, Lambda, CoreWeave, and the hyperscalers.

It is also the hour that survives a checkpoint failure, an eval job, a debug loop, and a serving process that has users. If the workload cannot die, on-demand is not a luxury. It is cheaper than restarting.

...

H100 is the card with the most mixed tables. Marketplace on-demand, marketplace spot, managed on-demand, hyperscaler on-demand, reserved. Same badge, five products. Start with how to rent an H100, then look at H100 vs H200 vs B200 only after the billing flag is honest.
